terminal_user_goal: Make the user's existing GameLoop PUBG Mobile installation actually render and run instead of presenting the persistent black screen, while preserving user data and avoiding speculative destructive changes.
why_selected: Live canonical state names END_TO_END_COMPUTER_WORK as the highest-leverage capability gap and requires real cross-domain mission pressure rather than qualification theater. The user has an unresolved real GameLoop/PUBG black-screen problem on the authorized Windows machine, so this mission simultaneously advances a real user goal and exercises computer-work diagnosis/action/verification.

falsifications_and_findings.hypothesis: The black screen is merely because the emulator never starts the PUBG package.
falsifications_and_findings.evidence: AndroidEmulator100.log reports StartPkgWithLogin for com.tencent.ig followed by OnAppRunning bRet=1 bRun=1 and OnGameStart.

falsifications_and_findings.hypothesis: The host GPU/OpenGL adapter is not detected.
falsifications_and_findings.evidence: AndroidEmulator100.log reports NVIDIA Corporation, RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, OpenGL 4.6.0 NVIDIA 595.71 and a matched render policy.

falsifications_and_findings.hypothesis: Switching the existing ForceDirectX registry flags from 0 to 1 is an adequate repair.
falsifications_and_findings.evidence: Both HKCU\Software\Tencent\MobileGamePC ForceDirectX flags were changed reversibly, PUBG relaunched, and a direct PrintWindow capture of the GameLoop main window remained fully black. The original values were restored to 0.

exact_observed_failure.repetition: AEngine100.log records repeated crash_type=4002 events for com.tencent.ig across multiple relaunch attempts.
exact_observed_failure.renderer_side_symptom: libOpenglRender.log repeatedly reports OpenFileMapping Global\AowShm-* Fail Error=2 while the main GameLoop render area remains black in direct window capture.

current_causal_frontier: Determine why com.tencent.ig repeatedly raises access violation 0xc0000005 in the Android/x86-64 execution path involving libc.so and libhotx612.so, and whether the trigger is the current PUBG native payload, GameLoop's ARM64 translation/runtime state, or a concrete dependency/loader mismatch. Do not perform more renderer toggles or reinstall/rename data until this crash boundary is resolved.
next_action: Recover and compare the exact current PUBG native-library payload and GameLoop translation/runtime artifacts against a known-good or official package/runtime state, using preserved files and hashes first; identify the first divergent library/dependency that is causally upstream of the libhotx612/libc access violation, then change only that component and replay once.
